comment: Canonical Hound-Up help content. A byte-for-byte copy of this file also lives at houndup-web/help-content.json — if you edit one, edit both. Written in plain, short-sentence UK English on purpose (aiming for an easy reading level), for both the in-app Help Centre and houndup-web/help.html.

articles.title: What is Hound-Up?
body: Hound-Up is an app for dog walkers. It helps you keep track of your clients, their dogs, your walks and sits, and your invoices.
It works fully on your phone, with no internet needed — even out on a walk with no signal. You'll sign in once with Apple to get started, and after that your data backs up automatically.

articles.title: Do I need to sign in?
body: Yes — you'll be asked to sign in with Apple the moment you open Hound-Up for the first time, before anything else. It's free and takes a few seconds.
Signing in is what keeps your clients, dogs, invoices, and your own business profile (name, rates, bank details) backed up and synced — so nothing's lost if you ever lose or replace your phone.
Autopilot adds extra automation on top of that — see "Free vs Autopilot" for the full list.

articles.title: Where does the weather come from?
body: The weather shown at the top of Today is based on the postcode saved in Business Details, not your phone's live location.
If it looks wrong, check that postcode is correct in Settings → Business Details.

articles.title: Adding your first client
body: Tap the + button on the Today tab, or go to the Dogs tab and tap "+ Dog".
You'll be asked for the dog's name and the owner's name and phone number. That's all you need to get started — you can fill in the rest of their details later.

articles.title: Adding a new client
body: Go to the Dogs tab and tap "+ Dog". Type the dog's name and the owner's details.
You can add more information later, like the owner's address, emergency contact, and any notes — just open the client's page and tap Edit.

articles.title: Adding a dog to an existing client
body: Open the client's page and tap the + next to Dogs. If they've already got one dog on file, this adds another one for the same owner — you won't need to type the owner's details again.

articles.title: Finding a client's address
body: When you're typing a client's address, start typing and a list of matching addresses will pop up. Tap the right one and it fills in the street, town and postcode for you.
Can't find it? Tap "Enter manually" underneath the search box and type the address in yourself.

articles.title: Adding a dog's vet
body: On a dog's page, tap Edit and use the "Search for a vet practice" box. If it finds the practice, it fills in the name and address for you.
If it can't find it, tap "Enter manually" and type the vet's name and address yourself.

articles.title: Editing a client or dog
body: Open the client or dog's page and tap Edit in the top corner. Change whatever you need, then tap Save.

articles.title: Logging a walk
body: Tap the + on Today (or Calendar's "Book…" button) and pick the service — one row per rate you've set up in Rates & Pricing, e.g. "Hourly Walk". Pick the dog, then the date.

The date decides what happens next: pick today or an earlier day and Hound-Up logs it as done and bills it straight away. Pick a day in the future and it's booked instead — nothing's charged until it actually happens. You can add a note or a photo too, if you like.

articles.title: Recording a walk live
body: Tap the + on Today and choose "Start a live walk". Hound-Up tracks your route using GPS while you walk, and you tap "Stop & save" when you're done.
This needs Hound-Up to know your location while you're recording — you'll be asked to allow this the first time.

articles.title: Booking a one-off walk
body: Tap a day on the Calendar tab and use the "Book…" button, or the + on Today. Pick the service and the dog, then choose a date in the future — Hound-Up books it in instead of billing it straight away.
This is for a single walk. If it's a regular booking, set up a schedule instead — see "Setting up a regular schedule".

articles.title: Setting up a regular schedule
body: Open a dog's page, go to the Schedule tab, and tap "Set a recurring schedule" (or "Add another schedule" if they've already got one). Pick the day of the week, the time, and how long the walk is.
Hound-Up creates each week's walk automatically, so you don't need to book it every time.

articles.title: Logging or booking a sit
body: Tap the + on Today (or Calendar's "Book…" button) and pick your overnight sit service, then the dog and the date. Sits can be a few hours or several days — Hound-Up bills by the night for anything longer than a day.
Same as a walk: today or an earlier date logs and bills it straight away; a future date books it instead.

articles.title: How invoicing works
body: Every walk and sit you log gets added to that client's running total, on the Ledger tab. When you're ready, you turn that total into an invoice and send it.
You don't have to invoice after every single walk — most walkers send one invoice a month for everything a client owes.

articles.title: Sending an invoice
body: Go to the Ledger tab, open a client's outstanding balance, and tap Send. Hound-Up emails the invoice to your client for you — there's no separate Mail app step needed.
To send it a different way instead — WhatsApp, AirDrop, or anything else on your phone — tap "Share invoice" and pick from your phone's usual share sheet.

articles.title: Getting paid by card or Apple Pay
body: Hound-Up can add a "Pay now" link to your invoices, so clients can pay you by card or Apple Pay. Set this up in Settings > Payment Details by connecting your own Stripe account.
The money goes straight into your own Stripe account — Hound-Up never touches it or takes a cut.

articles.title: Marking an invoice as paid
body: Open the invoice and tap "Mark as paid". If a client pays through your Stripe "Pay now" link, this happens automatically instead — whether or not you're on Autopilot. See "Free vs Autopilot".

articles.title: Nudging a late payment
body: On the Ledger tab, overdue invoices show a "Nudge" button — this sends a polite reminder. With Autopilot, this can also happen by itself, without you needing to open the app.

articles.title: Exporting your income for tax
body: Go to the Ledger tab and tap the export icon at the top. Choose a tax year (or your own date range) and Hound-Up creates a spreadsheet of everything you've earned, ready for your tax return or your accountant.

articles.title: What is the booking requests page?
body: It's the booking form built right into your microsite, so clients can ask you for a walk without phoning or texting you first — no separate link or page. It's an Autopilot feature — see "Free vs Autopilot".
Turn it on in Settings > Booking Availability. Share your micro-site link (Settings > Micro-site) to give clients access to it.

articles.title: Turning on your availability calendar
body: This shows clients which times you're actually free, right on your microsite's booking form, so they can just tap a time instead of guessing. Turn it on in Settings > Booking Availability.
It's just a helpful guide for clients — it doesn't stop two people picking the same time by accident, so you'll still want to check and confirm any request yourself.

articles.title: Accepting or declining a request
body: New requests show up as a notification in the app — tap it to see the details. If the person's already one of your clients, Hound-Up recognises them automatically and won't create a duplicate.
Tap Accept to book it in, or Decline if it doesn't work for you.

articles.title: What is Autopilot?
body: Autopilot is Hound-Up's paid tier — it keeps things running even with the app closed: nudging late payers, keeping your booking page and calendar feed live, and telling you straight away about a new booking request. You turn it on from Settings → Autopilot.
It's not a backup feature — your data already backs up automatically as soon as you sign in, whether or not you ever turn this on. See "Free vs Autopilot" for exactly what it adds.

articles.title: Free vs Autopilot
body: Hound-Up is free to use, with no limits on dogs, walks or invoices, and up to 10 active clients — everything backs up automatically and stays in sync across your devices from the moment you sign in. Autopilot is £9.99 a month on top, removes the 10-client cap, and adds a booking website with live availability booking plus auto-chasing overdue invoices even with the app closed. Here is exactly what is different.

articles.title: How do I upgrade to Autopilot?
body: Go to Settings > Autopilot and tap Upgrade. You'll see the price and what's included, then Apple's own payment screen — that's it, since you're already signed in.

articles.title: Managing or cancelling your subscription
body: Go to Settings > Autopilot and tap "Manage subscription" — this opens Apple's own subscription screen, where you can cancel or change it any time.

If you cancel, you keep everything until the end of the period you've already paid for. After that, Hound-Up goes back to working exactly like the free version — nothing is deleted, and your data keeps backing up exactly as before.

articles.title: Automatic backup
body: Hound-Up backs up your clients, dogs, walks, sits, invoices, ledger, and your own business profile automatically, the moment you're online — there's nothing to turn on.
This starts as soon as you sign in with Apple, which happens automatically the first time you open the app.
If you ever lose your phone or get a new one, sign in again and everything comes straight back.

articles.title: Backing up your data yourself
body: Go to Settings > Data and tap "Export all data". This saves everything — clients, dogs, walks, invoices, even photos — as one file you can save anywhere: Files, email, Google Drive, wherever you like.
This is completely free. Your data already backs up automatically (see "Automatic backup"), but this is a good extra copy to keep somewhere outside the app too.

articles.title: Recovering your data
body: If something on your phone looks out of date or missing — a client, a walk, an invoice — go to Settings > Data and tap "Recover" next to "Recover data". This pulls everything fresh from your account, straight over whatever's currently on this phone.

There's no separate restore-from-file step — "Export all data" (see "Backing up your data yourself") is a personal copy to keep outside the app, not something you re-import. Your account itself, via sign-in, is the real backup — that's what "Recover" pulls from.

articles.title: Erasing all your data
body: Go to Settings > Data and tap "Erase all data". This can't be undone, so Hound-Up will ask you to confirm first — it clears everything on this phone and deletes your account, including everything backed up to it.
If you just want to clear what's backed up to your account but keep everything on this phone, use "Delete cloud data" instead, further down the same screen.

articles.title: Turning on notifications
body: Go to Settings > Notifications to turn on things like a daily digest, invoicing reminders, or a push the moment you're paid. The first time you turn one on, Hound-Up will ask you to confirm before the phone's own permission prompt appears.

articles.title: What you get told about, and how
body: Hound-Up tells you about things in three ways: a bell icon in the app, a notification that pops up on your phone (even with the app shut), and sometimes an email. Not everything uses all three — here's how it works.

Getting paid is the simplest one — it always shows up in the bell icon and sends an email, and can pop up on your phone straight away for anyone who's turned that on in Settings. Free or Autopilot, it's the same.
A new booking request is different — receiving them at all is part of what Autopilot switches on, so that one's Autopilot-only, popping up on your phone the moment it arrives.

A question through your booking page ("Ask a question") is different again — anyone can receive those, free or Autopilot, and it always shows up in the bell icon and by email. The instant pop-up on your phone is the Autopilot part; on the free plan you'll just need to check the app instead of getting an alert.

Quieter jobs running in the background — like an automatic payment reminder or visit summary going out — only show up in the bell icon. They don't pop up on your phone. If several of these happened at once, a pop-up for every single one would just be annoying, so the bell icon is where they live instead.

articles.title: Daily digest
body: A single notification each morning summing up what's on today — how many walks, and anything that needs your attention. Turn it on in Settings > Notifications.

articles.title: Invoicing reminders
body: A reminder on the day of the month you choose, nudging you to send out invoices for everything logged that month. Turn it on and set the day in Settings > Notifications.
